title: Rest in the rule
hook: real rest, not only sleep: Antony showed a shocked hunter that a bow always bent will break
tomorrow: a man asked: tie my camel, or just trust God? what was the answer?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: here I am. Moses said hineni, and took off his shoes on holy ground. Today, a kind of rest that isn't sleep.

A work text on a Saturday: quick question. Two minutes to answer, and somehow the whole day tilts toward the inbox. A hunter in the Egyptian desert once had firm ideas about how holy people should spend their time. He came upon Abba Antony, the old hermit, sitting with the brothers, talking and enjoying their company, and he was shocked. Weren't monks supposed to be at prayer? Antony didn't argue. He turned to the hunter's bow.
screen: `QUICK QUESTION, ON A SATURDAY.` → `A HUNTER IN THE DESERT.` → `MONKS ENJOYING THEMSELVES?` → `ANTONY TURNS TO THE BOW.`

segments.voice: Put an arrow to the string, he said, and shoot. The hunter did. Shoot another. He did. Shoot again. And the hunter said: if I keep bending my bow like this, it will break. So it is with the work of God, Antony said. Stretch the brothers beyond measure and they'll soon break. Sometimes you have to come down and meet their needs. The hunter went away moved, and the brothers went home strengthened. Here's what the desert tradition made of it. The monks had a name for what Antony showed: discretion, the sense of measure. John Cassian, who carried the desert teaching to the West, tells of a time the elders asked which virtue keeps a monk from falling. Fasting? Keeping vigil? Giving everything away? Antony's answer was discretion, because it guards all the others. Without it, even good practice becomes a bow drawn until it snaps. So in the desert, rest that isn't sleep, a meal together, talk, an easy hour with the brothers, wasn't a lapse from the work of God. It was part of it. A bow doesn't rest by being left strung in a corner. It rests when the string comes off. Real rest in your rule is time when nothing is pulling at you, no quick questions, no inbox, so that when you draw again, it holds.
screen: `SHOOT. SHOOT AGAIN.` · `A BOW ALWAYS BENT WILL BREAK.` · `DISCRETION: THE SENSE OF MEASURE.` · `REST IS PART OF THE WORK.` · then, large: `REST.`

segments.voice: Put your phone out of reach and let your hands rest open on your lap, like a bow with the string taken off. For the whole sit, do nothing useful. If a to-do comes up, let it wait like a letter on the table, unopened. Notice what your body does when nothing is asked of it.
Rest in the rule: time written in when nothing is pulling at you, not only sleep, the way Antony showed the hunter an unstrung bow.
Your line: rest. Antony said a bow always bent will break, so take the string off. See you tomorrow, day 1651.

howItsDone: The desert monks prized discretion, the sense of measure, and kept time for rest and company alongside prayer. Some people on other paths keep a weekly day or evening free of work and screens.
